mechanism_narrative: The steady week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC over the last four weeks (-19.0 to -17.7) reflects an ongoing recovery trend in discretionary outings that will continue mechanically into the next four weeks absent any shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose each of the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, reversing the observed monotonic uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-week jump in PARKS mobility (-16.0 to -12.6) signals rising outdoor leisure activity that spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits within one to two weeks as people combine errands with outdoor trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS increased 3.4 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following a PARKS jump exceeding 3 points, or declines despite the PARKS surge persisting.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility staying near 15% above baseline indicates continued time-at-home behavior that substitutes for in-person retail visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks even as other indicators improve.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained between 14.6 and 15.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining flat or elevated above 14 points.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -25 (a threshold indicating meaningfully reduced commuting suppression), the associated increase in people moving through transit hubs will drive a corresponding rise in nearby retail and recreation footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -25.0 from its current -28.0 level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -30.3 to -28.0 over the snapshot
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -25.0 but RETAIL_REC does not rise within the following two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises without TRANSIT crossing the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility signals a coordinated policy-driven relaxation of restrictions, which jointly amplifies retail recovery beyond what either series alone would predict, because commuting and shopping trips are chained together.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -17.1 to -15.6 while TRANSIT improved from -30.3 to -28.0 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks is no greater than the growth predicted from WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The uptick in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS together in the most recent week suggests a seasonal shift (e.g., holiday or weather-driven) toward outdoor and errand activity that will also lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as part of a broader seasonal mobility increase.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -2.0 to 2.3 and PARKS rose from -14.9 to -12.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite continued or stable gains in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS, indicating no shared seasonal driver.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above 16 points while WORKPLACES simultaneously declines, this signals a renewed stay-at-home regime (e.g., precautionary behavior or restriction tightening) that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 16.0 and WORKPLACES declines week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL currently at 14.6 and WORKPLACES at -15.6, both near recent stable levels
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL crosses above 16.0 with WORKPLACES declining but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The one-week acceleration in RETAIL_REC's rate of improvement (from +0.4 to +1.0 point gains week-on-week) indicates building momentum in consumer activity that will produce a further near-term rise in RETAIL_REC within the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC gained 1.0 point from t-1w to t-0w versus 0.4 the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show a further weekly gain exceeding the prior week's gain in the next observed week, or it declines.
